blocks.x: Size-curve allocation rebuilt on sensing, sell-through up 9 points and transfer volume between stores down 24%

A fashion retailer: Retail chains feel decision gaps in margin per store, visible in the weekly numbers. The Achala program started with the pricing and availability flow —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline season measured the churn: 71% full-price sell-through on core lines but 52% on new drops, inter-store transfers running 31% of volume, and the allocation team defending a one-size-fits-many curve.
Local demand signals existed in POS history but allocation ran on chain-level curves. Size availability failures at the fitting room never surfaced to the people buying the sizes.

We rebuilt allocation on sensing: store-cluster size curves learned from POS and returns, drops allocated to store-cluster demand with fit-signal feedback, transfer recommendations only when curves genuinely diverged from stock, and the buying team reviewing curve accuracy each season. The fitting-room failure became a measurable, managed event.
